author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces
summary: The machine-readable veterinarian directory route becomes a supported surface, and both directory surfaces accept an optional whole-name, case-insensitive specialty filter. Absent or blank filter preserves today's behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The machine-readable form of the directory returns the same veterinarians and specialties as a supported surface, not an unrequested artifact
Filtering the directory page by a specialty at least one veterinarian holds lists only those veterinarians, still a page at a time
Filtering the machine-readable form by a specialty at least one veterinarian holds returns only those veterinarians
Matching is on the whole specialty name and ignores letter case; a value that is only the start of a specialty name does not match
A specialty no veterinarian holds returns the normal result with an empty veterinarian list and a successful response, not an error, on both surfaces
An empty or whitespace-only filter value behaves as if no filter were supplied, like an empty owner search
With no filter supplied both surfaces behave exactly as REQ-VET-001 specifies
non_goals: Free-text search over veterinarians (NG-9, narrowed) — the filter narrows an already-displayed attribute, it does not add a search surface
notes: Supersedes withdrawn REQ-VET-002 (id retired, not reused). Concrete surface mechanism (the specialty query parameter, the two route paths, the successful-response status code) is the design stage's to place in system-design.md; the PRD states behavior only. The docs/adr/README.md index is owned by system-design-expert and does not yet list adr/2026-08-05-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md — add it when that agent next edits the index.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty filter is a small extension of the recorded owner last-name search pattern (system-design.md#contracts): OwnerController.processFindForm + OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) is the precedent for filter-a-list-and-page-it. Applied to vets, the filter becomes a Spring Data derived query on VetRepository over the Vet.specialties many-to-many, and VetController's existing findPaginated helper gains the filter argument. No new module, type, pattern, or dependency; the domain model (Vet/Specialty) is unchanged. system-design.md updated: VetController/VetRepository/Vets contract rows re-scoped to REQ-VET-003, and the Known Defects row that marked the machine-readable route pending-removal removed (REQ-VET-003 now makes it a supported surface).
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived-query overloads mirroring the existing findAll pair: Page<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) for the HTML surface and Collection<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) for the JSON surface. IgnoreCase (whole-name equality, no StartingWith) satisfies case-insensitive whole-name matching and rejects prefixes; Distinct guards the many-to-many join. Annotate consistently with the existing findAll methods (@Transactional(readOnly=true), @Cacheable("vets")) — vet data has no write path so caching filtered results is safe; leaving them uncached is also acceptable.

VetController: both handlers gain @RequestParam(required=false) String specialty. Mirror owner search's blank handling — strip the value; if null/empty after strip, take the unfiltered path (existing findAll / findAll(pageable)), else the filtered query. Paging composes over the filtered result set because the derived query takes the Pageable, so totalPages/totalItems reflect the filtered count.

vetList.html: pagination links currently hard-code /vets.html?page=N and would drop the active filter. Rebuild them with a Thymeleaf URL expression binding both params, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}, and add specialty to the model. This preserves the filter across pages (required by 'still a page at a time' on the filtered list) and gives correct URL-encoding + escaping of the user value. No filter input form is required — the filter is a query parameter per the product owner; only link preservation is needed.

patterns.description: processFindForm: strip the search term, treat blank as the broadest result, page the filtered list — the blank-handling and pagination shape to mirror for specialty
findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable): the derived-query + Pageable precedent for filter-and-page; the vet filter is the whole-name IgnoreCase analogue

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is @ManyToMany(fetch=EAGER); a derived query combining an eager collection with a Pageable can trigger Hibernate's in-memory-pagination warning (HHH000104) or a collection-fetch-with-paging path, which can distort counts.
risks.mitigation: Assert filtered totalElements/totalPages in VetControllerTests against a seeded dataset spanning more than one page. If the warning or a wrong count appears, express the query as an explicit @Query selecting distinct vets with a separate count query, or filter distinct vet ids first. In-memory filtering over the already-cached findAll() collection is the fallback mechanism if the DB-side query proves awkward — equally correct for this tiny, cached dataset.

risks.risk: The specialty value is reflected into pagination hrefs and reaches the DB.
risks.mitigation: DB path is a parameterized derived query (no injection). Href path uses the Thymeleaf @{...(param=...)} URL expression, which URL-encodes the param and escapes output by default — no string concatenation into the URL.

notes: No ADR for the filter mechanism: the repository-query-vs-in-memory choice, the IgnoreCase whole-name match, and Pageable composition are all routine applications of the recorded owner-search pattern — reversible, no cross-cutting trade-off, no new dependency. The product-level decision (narrow NG-9; the machine-readable surface becomes supported) already has its non-goal ADR at docs/adr/2026-08-05-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md, now added to docs/adr/README.md. Carried-forward items both done: ADR index entry added; filter-mechanism ADR judged unwarranted. No design-doc-autofix records present, so the autofix audit is a silent skip. Foundational five-signal check: none trip — mature codebase with recorded architecture, ADRs, and confirmed vocabulary.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Both new specialty-filter query overloads are @Cacheable("vets"), and the SimpleKeyGenerator keys them on the raw user-supplied specialty string. The "vets" cache is configured with an unbounded MutableConfiguration (no size limit, no TTL; the config comment itself notes the size limit is left unset). VetController.normalize() only trims whitespace and nulls empties -- it does not bound length, cardinality, or validate the value against known specialties. Because the endpoints have no authentication (NG-1), any caller can issue GET /vets.html?specialty=<distinct> or GET /vets?specialty=<distinct> with unlimited distinct values, each inserting a permanent entry into the unbounded cache and growing the heap without limit (memory-exhaustion / availability). Remediation is a policy decision (escalate): either (a) drop @Cacheable from the two user-keyed overloads -- the existing findAll() caching is unaffected, or (b) bound the "vets" cache with a Caffeine size/TTL spec, or (c) validate specialty against the finite set of known specialty names before querying/caching.

approved_aspects: No SQL/JPQL injection: findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase is a Spring Data derived query, fully parameterized (no string concatenation)

No reflected XSS / URL injection: specialty is rendered only inside Thymeleaf @{/vets.html(...)} link expressions, which URL-encode parameter values and HTML-escape the href attribute; it is never emitted as body text or via th:utext

No cache key collision or poisoning across the four @Cacheable("vets") methods: SimpleKeyGenerator yields distinct key types (SimpleKey.EMPTY, Pageable, String, SimpleKey(String,Pageable)); empties normalize to null so filtered calls cannot overwrite unfiltered findAll() entries
Reinstated JSON /vets endpoint exposes no data beyond the HTML vet list (same Vet/specialty fields)
NG-1 no-auth posture judged as recorded in docs/system-design.md#security-context, not re-litigated

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: Format check passes cleanly (checkFormat UP-TO-DATE, no violations)

VetRepository new overloads mirror the existing findAll pair exactly — same @Transactional(readOnly=true) and @Cacheable("vets") annotations, same throws DataAccessException clause, same Javadoc style; cache key collisions are impossible because Spring's default key generator distinguishes type and arity across all four methods

normalize() is a single-responsibility private helper with a clear Javadoc that explains the null-as-absent contract; early return, no side effects, uses String.strip() (Unicode-safe, Java 17 appropriate)
findPaginated(int, String) follows the early-return-for-no-filter pattern with the happy path last — consistent with the existing owner search structure

vetList.html pagination links correctly replaced from string-interpolation hrefs to Thymeleaf @{} URL expressions carrying specialty=${specialty}; Thymeleaf omits the parameter when the model value is null, so unfiltered pages produce clean /vets.html?page=N links without a spurious specialty= fragment
model.addAttribute("specialty", filter) placed before addPaginationModel ensures the attribute is in scope for the template on the same model object

showResourcesVetList uses this.vetRepository consistently within the method for both the filtered and unfiltered branch — the pre-existing this. discrepancy between methods is not introduced by this change

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Test name `shouldFilterVetListPageByWholeSpecialtyNameIgnoringCase` promises case-insensitive matching, but the specialty parameter passed is already lowercase `"radiology"`. The test exercises filtered paging and model attributes — correct and valuable — but it does not demonstrate the case-insensitivity it advertises. A future reader relying on the name as specification would be misled. Either rename to `shouldFilterVetListPageByWholeSpecialtyName` and let the integration test own the case-insensitivity proof, or replace `"radiology"` with a mixed-case value (e.g. `"RaDiOlOgY"`) and add a corresponding stub for that exact string.
findings.fix: Rename to `shouldFilterVetListPageByWholeSpecialtyName`, removing the `IgnoringCase` claim the test body does not support. If the case-insensitive controller-layer path is wanted here, change the specialty param to `"RaDiOlOgY"` and stub `eq("RaDiOlOgY")` instead.

findings.description: Bare literals `8` (total element count) and `5` (page size) in `new PageImpl<>(filtered, PageRequest.of(0, 5), 8)` make the derivation `ceil(8/5) = 2 pages` invisible. The assertions that follow (`totalItems: 8L`, `totalPages: 2`) appear as magic numbers; a reader cannot verify them without mental arithmetic. Extract to named locals such as `int FILTERED_TOTAL = 8; int PAGE_SIZE = 5;` and derive `expectedPages = (int) Math.ceil((double) FILTERED_TOTAL / PAGE_SIZE)` or simply inline the derivation in the assertion.
findings.fix: Replace bare `8` and `5` with named locals that make the page-count derivation self-evident.

findings.description: The comment `// The filtered set is paged, so the unfiltered directory query is never used.` restates exactly what the immediately following `verify(this.vets, never()).findAll(any(Pageable.class))` already says. The testing-principles brief prohibits inline prose that narrates obvious logic. Remove it.

The comment `// A blank filter takes the unfiltered path; the filtered query is never issued.` restates the two `verify(this.vets, never())` assertions that follow. Same prohibition as above. Remove it.

approved_aspects: All nine Done-when criteria for REQ-VET-003 are covered: machine-readable surface as supported route (shouldServeMachineReadableVetDirectoryAsSupportedSurface), filtered HTML paging (shouldFilterVetListPageByWholeSpecialtyNameIgnoringCase), filtered JSON (shouldFilterVetJsonBySpecialty), unmatched specialty → empty + 200 on both surfaces (shouldReturnEmptyVetListForUnmatchedSpecialtyWithSuccess), blank/whitespace filter treated as absent on both surfaces (shouldTreatBlankSpecialtyFilterAsAbsent), and no-filter behavior covered by pre-existing tests

Layering call for PetClinicIntegrationTests is correct: case-insensitive whole-name matching and prefix rejection are Spring Data derived-query semantics compiled by the JPA provider; a controller test with a stubbed repo cannot prove the DB-level contract. shouldMatchWholeSpecialtyNameIgnoringCase and shouldNotMatchSpecialtyByPrefix belong in a real-I/O integration test

Multi-page count test (shouldReflectFilteredCountWhenPagingFilteredVets) genuinely exercises more than one page: PageRequest.of(0,1) against two seeded radiology vets forces firstPage.totalPages==2, firstPage.content.size==1, secondPage.content.size==1, and distinct IDs across pages. The HHH000104 risk is non-vacuously addressed
Mocking policy is compliant: @MockitoBean VetRepository under @WebMvcTest is the sanctioned web-layer boundary mock; PetClinicIntegrationTests injects the real repository against real H2
AssertJ fluent assertions used throughout; MockMvc matchers used correctly for the web layer
verify(never()) guards correctly prevent silent fallback to the unfiltered query path in every filtered-path test
